name: Fired clay type
summary: Bi Sheng's separate clay characters, each carved and hardened by firing so they could be arranged into pages and reused, as described by Shen Gua.
description: Bi Sheng’s separately carved clay characters, hardened by firing, as reported by Shen Gua.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.

date.basis: Shen Gua retrospectively attributes the reported workflow to the Qingli reign; anchor is only a display midpoint.

evidence.supports: Tsien translates and reproduces the particular historical passage that describes fired separate clay characters; the image caption dates its source edition to the fourteenth century.
Modern translation of the same account describes fired separate clay characters.

date.label: by late 11th century (Shen Gua’s account)
date.basis: Shen’s late-eleventh-century account places retention after Bi Sheng’s death; the transfer date is not specified.

events.statement: Shen Gua reports that his nephews obtained Bi Sheng’s types after Bi died and preserved them until the time of his writing.
events.caveats: This is textual testimony of retention, not evidence that the family printed with the types, transmitted the method to later printers, or preserved them to the present.

links.statement: Is woodblock practice a documented precursor of Bi Sheng's type? All three print entries are separate.
links.caveats: Evidence needed: Shen Kuo's account and print histories.
links.finding: The 868 Diamond Sutra is one woodblock-printed scroll; Shen describes earlier woodblock practice and later Bi Sheng movable types. These passages do not identify the particular Diamond Sutra copy as an input to Bi Sheng or establish a causal path from that object. Generic historical antecedence is not an object-specific development edge.

research.note: Independent reader checked the modern translation of Shen Gua’s account: his nephews obtained and retained the types after Bi died; later use is not established.
